title: Which crane opens its beak to the bigger angle?
description: Two cranes argue about who opens a mouth wider. Both beak angles are traced, and one transparent circle is placed on each with its centre on the vertex. The gaps between the marked points on the circle are compared, and Keeko's doubt is that the wider gap between the beak tips is the bigger angle.
teaching_notes: One idea: compare the two gaps on the same circle, both measured at the same distance from the vertex. Watch for students who compare the gap between the beak tips on the page, which changes with the length of the beak.

source: Which crane was making the bigger angle? If you can make a c
video_script.why: The child decides which of two angles is bigger by comparing two gaps on the same transparent circle.
video_script.substitution: the book's two cranes and the transparent circle
video_script.anchor: the two cranes of the book, with a transparent circle on each beak angle
video_script.wrong_answer: the wider gap between the beak tips is the bigger angle
video_script.wrong_move: compares the gap between the beak tips on the page instead of the gap on one circle
video_script.payoff_line: The crane whose marked points are farther apart makes the bigger angle

final_answer.value: the crane whose marked points on the circle are farther apart makes the bigger angle
final_answer.spoken: the crane whose marked points on the circle are farther apart makes the bigger angle

maths_rules: trace each beak angle with its vertex marked
place the transparent circle with its centre on the vertex and mark A and B where the arms cross the edge
place the same circle on the other angle with its centre on that vertex and one arm through A, then mark where the other arm crosses
compare the two gaps between marked points on the same circle
the angle whose marked points are farther apart is the bigger angle
slip: the gap between beak tips on the page changes with the length of the beak, but the angle does not
video_script.design: One idea: one circle, two gaps, and the larger gap is the bigger angle. The two cranes and the circle stay on the board. Keeko's doubt: the wider gap between the beak tips is the bigger angle.
open_questions: Which of the two cranes makes the bigger angle depends on the book's picture, which could not be viewed; the video gives the method only.
